Rayan Cherki, Man City midfielder, TNT Sports:.

Which Premier League players are set for yellow card suspensions?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (567 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yeremy Pino is the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow-card suspension.
  • Crystal Palace's Yeremy Pino has become the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow card suspension after accumulating five bookings since the 2026-27 season began.
  • Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash were the first players to receive a ban for collecting five yellow cards before gameweek 19.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yeremy Pino is the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow-card suspension.

Crystal Palace's Yeremy Pino has become the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow card suspension after accumulating five bookings since the 2026-27 season began.

Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash were the first players to receive a ban for collecting five yellow cards before gameweek 19.

Players receive a one-match suspension if they pick up five or more yellow cards prior to the conclusion of their team's 19th league match of the season.

There are now 17 players sitting on four bookings after 11 rounds of matches, meaning they must avoid another yellow card prior to the halfway point of the season to avoid a ban.

Bournemouth have the most players on the brink of a ban, with three players one yellow card away from suspension.

After that date, the threshold increases to 10 yellow cards. Any player reaching that number before the end of their club's 32nd league match of the season will receive a two-match suspension.

From that point, there are further thresholds at 15 and 20 yellow cards.

For players reaching 15 cautions, they incur a three-match suspension. Punishments for players reaching 20 yellow cards are determined by a regulatory commission.

Those cut-offs do not reset until the end of the Premier League season.

In the Championship, League One and League Two, there are similar thresholds.

However, with those three divisions having 46 rounds of league matches instead of 38, players have to avoid getting 10 yellow cards before the end of the 37th league match in order to not receive a two-match suspension.

In those divisions, the yellow cards are reset at the end of the league season and do not include matches in the play-offs.

The following players have received a one-match ban and will now receive a two-match ban if they reach ten bookings before game week 32:.

Yeremy Pino - Crystal Palace (five yellow cards).

Matt Crooks - Hull City (five yellow cards).

Matty Cash - Aston Villa (five).

If any of the following players receive another Premier League yellow card before the season's halfway point, they will be banned for one match:.

Vitaly Janelt - Brentford (four).

Oli McBurnie - Hull City (four).

Harry Maguire - Manchester United (four).

Pascal Gross - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Ethan Ampadu - Leeds United (four).

Oliver Boscagli - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Adam Smith - Bournemouth (four).

Marcus Tavernier - Bournemouth (four).

Antonio Silva - Bournemouth (four).

Alexis Mac Allister - Liverpool (four).

James McAtee - Nottingham Forest (four).

Chema Andres - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Bradley Barcola - Liverpool (four).

Murillo - Nottingham Forest (four).

The following players will miss their club's next set of fixtures:.

Yeremy Pino - Crytsal Palce (yellow card suspension).

Jean-Philippe Mateta - Crystal Palace (red card suspension).

Igor Thiago - Brentford (red card suspension).

Costinha - Brighton & Hove Albion (red card suspension).

Leny Yoro - Manchester United (red card suspension).

James Tarkowski - Everton (red card suspension).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there are two non-negotiables for Chelsea managers. Do not lose at home to Tottenham Hotspur and do not lose at home to Leeds United. But Xabi Alonso has now completed the nightmare double.

Just as Spurs broke their Stamford Bridge hoodoo a few weeks ago, Leeds secured their first win at Chelsea since 1999 by humiliating the hosts after falling a goal behind.

It was 67 long years since Chelsea had last lost at home to Tottenham and Leeds in the same season, and Alonso was left in no doubt about how seriously supporters take that as his team were loudly booed and he was heckled.

Cole Palmer stormed down the tunnel at full time, ignoring the advice of Chelsea’s so-called “cultural architect” Willie Isa to applaud the remaining home fans, and shrugging off the attention of injured striker João Pedro.

Having been left out of the last England squad, Palmer was largely anonymous for Chelsea but he was not alone and Alonso is already facing similar questions to his predecessors about the team’s mentality.

According to recent reports, “I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment, mentally,” Alonso said. “When we receive a punch, we didn’t recover that strong, that tough enough and today that was my feeling.

“The fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high and we feel sorry for them. For sure, it’s not the easiest moment. It’s a fragile moment, but we need to work together and stick together because there is still a long way to go.”.

Alonso is yet to name the same starting XI for successive league games and there appears to be no discernible blueprint or style of play.

Injuries have contributed to Chelsea’s unremarkable start to the season under Alonso – and Moisés Caicedo was forced off early in the first half – but the problems run deeper than the treatment table.

Recent findings suggest that alonso’s defence has now conceded 20 goals, which has contributed to Chelsea losing five league games already – more than Manchester United. In between three defeats in their last four league games, Chelsea were also knocked out of the Carabao Cup.

The Spaniard had answered questions about Chelsea’s identity, or lack of it, by saying he wanted his team to be competitive. But they were anything but against a Leeds side who had seven more shots than their hosts and five more on target.

It is hard to fathom how, through all the chopping and changing, Wesley Fofana still starts games for Chelsea in defence. It was his pathetic attempted header, which bounced backwards towards his own goal, that contributed to Noah Okafor’s first goal.

Josh Acheampong also got himself into a mess and Okafor was somehow able to squeeze a shot past goalkeeper Emi Martínez despite having three Chelsea players around him.

Chelsea had taken the lead through striker Emmanuel Emegha, on his first start for the club, but from that moment on they were second best with Leeds pair Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka running the middle of the park.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin had hit the crossbar and failed to find the net with three more presentable opportunities in the first half, but he took his chance from the penalty spot eight minutes after the break.

Morgan Rogers had argued that James Justin’s shot hit him too far up his arm for it to be a penalty, but a VAR check upheld referee Michael Oliver’s decision and Calvert-Lewin kept his cool.

That should have been the moment that shook Chelsea into action and prompted a response but, instead, Alonso’s team fell apart and he was unable to provoke a shift in momentum from the touchline.

Just five minutes after Calvert-Lewin had put Leeds ahead, Okafor effectively sealed the victory by firing the ball into the net after Chelsea had failed to deal with a long throw into their penalty area.

According to recent reports, noah Okafor's brace helps seal Leeds' first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge since 1999! 💥 https://t.co/UAmsJziJmZ.

Recent findings suggest that “I can’t wait to be on the sofa with coffee and cake and also watch this game back because it was a really good game,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds head coach, said. “I was a bit disappointed even at half-time when it was just a draw, because I think we were the better side from the first to the last.”.

John Terry still works with Chelsea’s academy and it might be worth Alonso getting the former captain to speak to the club’s senior players about how to defend and compete. Whatever has been done on the training pitch so far has not worked.

Alonso’s substitutes are yet to register a single goal or assist in the league this season and his changes failed to make any sort of impact here. For the visitors, however, two substitutes combined to score their fourth goal in time added on for stoppages.

Harry Wilson played in Brenden Aaronson and, from a tight angle, he managed to find the back of the net by sending the ball through the legs of Martínez.

The home stands were already half-empty by that point, but some supporters hung around to show their displeasure and Palmer could not contain his anger.

It has been revealed that we know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect - we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It’s right we can enjoy this performance.

What a day for Leeds. They scored four and it could have been more. For Chelsea, they lost their way when Caicedo went off and without Joao Pedro, they have lost their spark in attack.

Thomas Frank declared “it’s good to be back in the circus” of football management ahead of his first match as Crystal Palace boss.

The 53-year-old Dane admitted he could have easily spent a few more months sipping wine, “eating too well” and collecting passport stamps, but something resonated when he asked his wife why he was tempted to seek out a new job and she told him, “(It’s) because you can’t help yourself”.

Frank hinted that there was more behind the story to his disappointing spell at Tottenham he might one day reveal, but for now he has a team to rescue from a relegation fight, beginning with today’s trip to Coventry.

If you don’t learn from any of your jobs, I don’t think you reflect, I don’t think you improve, and I don’t think you get better.

Recent findings suggest that of course there’s a lot of things I have been reflecting over. The details, that will be for another time, but I can say I’ve learned, definitely.

I was very aware I didn’t want to do anything in the summer. I put a statement out there, I needed more time. I can actually, honestly say I would have been fine if it was three, four, five, six, seven months more, because it’s good to be back in the circus, but it’s also unbelievably good not to be in, especially if you enjoy life, which I do.

I was spending time with family and friends and doing all that, but I think the club, the way Palace is, how well Steve Parish especially spoke about the club and ideas, Matt Hobbs and Iain Moody and these guys, too, helped convince me it was a good idea.

There are clear structural changes since Villa’s last home game and a mural of fans makes it more appealing to look at.

This stand is scheduled to be ready for next season and will increase Villa’s capacity to over 50,000.

De Zerbi made six changes from the aforementioned defeat to Leeds, including a first start for teenager Luca Williams-Barnett, a player who has come through the club’s academy.

There is no place in the squad for Sandro Tonali or Tosin Adarabioyo, but James Maddison will start for the first time since the 2-0 defeat to Chelsea in October.

Aston Villa 2.0 was always likely to be a slow-burner, and it is proving exactly that for Unai Emery.

His team has impressed and underwhelmed in equal measure so far this season but this is an opportunity to hoist themselves up the table.

A clean sheet would be a good starting point, as they have not secured a shutout in front of their own fans in the league since March.

Tottenham teenager Luca Williams-Barnett has committed his future to his boyhood club by signing a latest contract.

The 18-year-old caught the eye during his full Spurs debut in Saturday's 2-0 Premier League victory over Ipswich, striking after 15 minutes before driving forward from deep inside his own half to assist Dominic Solanke six minutes after the second-half restart.

With his previous agreement entering its final 24 months, Spurs have now moved to extend the youngster's contract.

"This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach, but this is only the start," the Academy graduate told the official club website.

Sources indicate that "Spurs is a family to me. I have been here for so long – it’s a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

"The club has trusted and believed in me, now I’m ready to repay that.".

Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi believes far more is to come from the England Under-19 international.

"Luca is a player I think the world of, and I’m so happy that he has signed a new contract," De Zerbi stated.

"He has benefitted from being around the first team every day, growing in stature and consistency, and has deserved his place in the matchday squad over recent weeks.

"Everyone can see how technically gifted Luca is on the pitch, but I also love his calmness and decision-making under pressure.

Industry observers note that "The best players have confidence on the pitch and humility off it. There is still plenty of room for Luca to improve, and I know he will continue to work hard every day to be the best version of himself.".

Spurs sporting director Johan Lange feels "special talent" Williams-Barnett fully merits his fresh contract.

"Luca’s progression through the Academy to this point is a great example of what our pathway is designed to achieve and what is possible for young players here," Lange said.

"We are excited to watch Luca continue to develop and be an vital player for the club, both in the present and the future.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Following a disappointing start to the campaign and the arrival of a latest regulatory era in English football, the club’s latest financial results offer a clear picture as to how much room INEOS actually have to manoeuvre.
  • Man United’s most recent full-year accounts, covering the 12-month period to 30 June, 2026, which were published in September, paints a picture of cost-cutting paired with historically strong commercial standing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has barely unpacked his bags at Old Trafford, but it's already abundantly clear Manchester United need to back their newly introduced head coach in January.

Following a disappointing start to the campaign and the arrival of a latest regulatory era in English football, the club’s latest financial results offer a clear picture as to how much room INEOS actually have to manoeuvre.

Man United’s most recent full-year accounts, covering the 12-month period to 30 June, 2026, which were published in September, paints a picture of cost-cutting paired with historically strong commercial standing.

Despite having no European football last season, Man United posted record revenue of £677.6 million while trimming wages for a third consecutive year to £302.0m.

Although previous recruitment pushed player amortisation to £211.8m and left a net loss of £43.0m after finance costs, £47.0m in player-sale profits kept the underlying business moving forward.

Even more telling are Man United’s first-quarter results for 2026/27, released on November 19.

With Champions League football back at Old Trafford, quarterly revenue rose 4.1 per cent to £146.1m, and the club are predicted to earn £740m and £760m annually.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Quarterly player amortisation fell by almost 15 per cent following summer exits and Casemiro’s contract expiry, while another £20.7m was banked in player-disposal profits.

This summer, the Premier League replaced Profitability and Sustainability Rules (PSR) with its newly introduced Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) system. Under SCR, clubs’ on-pitch spending - which comprises first-team player and head coach wages, transfer amortisation, and agent fees, while excluding non-playing staff, academy and women’s team costs - is capped at 85 per cent of football revenue plus net profit on player sales.

There is even a 30 per cent multi-year buffer up to a 115 per cent ‘Red Threshold’ before points deductions apply. However, because Man United are competing in the Champions League, they must simultaneously adhere to UEFA’s stricter 70 per cent squad cost limit ahead of the March 1 compliance checkpoint.

Therefore, Pochettino has far more breathing room in the transfer market than naysayers might suggest.

Taking the £750m midpoint of Man United’s expected 2026/27 revenue and adding roughly £45m - which is an average of player-trading profits over recent years - that gives an adjusted revenue figure of £795m.

Under the Premier League’s 85 per cent threshold, Man United could carry £675.8m in annual squad costs. Under UEFA’s tighter 70 per cent ceiling, their limit sits at £556.5m.

It has been revealed that remove non-playing staff from total wages and Man United’s first-team player and coaching bill sits near £255m. Add £186.4m in annualised amortisation and roughly £35m in agents’ fees, and total squad costs land around £476.4m - roughly 60 per cent of adjusted revenue.

That leaves roughly £80m in annual squad-cost headroom beneath UEFA’s 70 per cent cap - and nearly £200m domestically.

This means Man United could comfortably sanction £120m to £150m in winter transfer spending. That remarked, their borrowing position and existing credit facility could yet prove to be a handbrake on any January rebuild, but from a purely regulatory standpoint, Man United's transfer expenditure picture is a rosy one.

England are a seeded side for the Nations League quarter-finals after topping their group.

The draw for the final eight teams in the 2026-27 Nations League will be on Friday, 20 November at 11:00 GMT.

It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.

England are the only home nation to have made it to the quarter-final stage, however Northern Ireland's draw against Hungary saw them top Group B2 and secure promotion to League A in the 2028-29 tournament.

Scotland will remain in League B following their third-place finish in Group B1, and Wales face a League A/B relegation play-off in March after being consigned to last place in Group A4.

The Republic of Ireland finished second in Group B3 and so will take part in a League A/B promotion play-off in March.

The winners of groups A1-A4 are seeded for the draw, playing the runners-up of other groups in League A.

England have sealed their place in the last eight as Group A3 winners and could face:.

They cannot face A3 runners-up Spain as teams must be drawn against sides from other groups.

The quarter-finals will be played over two legs during the international break between 25-30 March.

Seeded teams get to play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.

Nations that reach the semi-finals can bid those penultimate matches as well as the final.

The remaining dates for the Nations League are:.

Quarter-finals first leg: 25-27 March.

Quarter-finals second leg: 28-30 March.

Semi-finals, third-place play-off and final: 9-13 June.

Germany's flagship airline Lufthansa plans to cut 1,000 jobs at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs, according to a organization letter seen by German news agency DPA and news outlets.

The letter was reportedly signed by Lufthansa CEO Jens Ritter and four other board members.

This is reportedly down to ongoing financial losses. In the first nine months of the year, the airline recorded an operating loss of €180 million ($197 million).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that the executive board noted on average the loss amounts to €20 million every month, according to media reports. The board stated in the letter that "this is the third year in a row of not being financially successful.".

"Lufthansa is right now not competitive in terms of its cost structure, efficiency and productivity," the letter said.

At the end of 2025, the Lufthansa group employed some 67,100 people, up 1% from the previous year.

The company also looks to cut employee travel benefits, restructure its hub operations to reduce crew overnight stays abroad, and reduce short- and medium-haul capacity by replacing some A320 aircraft with A220 jets.

Furthermore, it prepares to equip ten aircraft per month with Starlink, a satellite internet service developed by tech billionaire Elon Musk. The airline hopes to generate "additional revenue” by monetizing onboard internet access, according to the letter.

Sources indicate that the time frame of the cuts is unclear. It's also unknown whether the cuts were a part of a previously confirmed downsizing.

In September 2025, Lufthansa said it would slash 4,000 administrative positions due to the implementation of AI and digitalization.

In regards to this year, Lufthansa has faced rising fuel costs spurred by the US-Israeli war with Iran, further complicating its financial outlook.

Industry News: Kwame Brathwaite, photographer of 'Black is Beautiful' movement, dies at 85

📅 04 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 4 min read (768 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Editor’s Note:  This article was originally published by The Art Newspaper, an editorial partner of CNN Style.
  • Kwame Brathwaite, the pioneering activist and photographer whose work helped define the aesthetics of the “Black is Beautiful” movement of the 1960s and beyond, died on April 1, aged 85.
  • His son, Kwame Brathwaite, Jr, announced his father’s death in an Instagram post that read in part, “I am deeply saddened to share that my Baba, the patriarch of our family, our rock and my hero has transitioned.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor’s Note:  This article was originally published by The Art Newspaper, an editorial partner of CNN Style.

Kwame Brathwaite, the pioneering activist and photographer whose work helped define the aesthetics of the “Black is Beautiful” movement of the 1960s and beyond, died on April 1, aged 85.

His son, Kwame Brathwaite, Jr, announced his father’s death in an Instagram post that read in part, “I am deeply saddened to share that my Baba, the patriarch of our family, our rock and my hero has transitioned.”.

Brathwaite’s work has been the subject of resurgent interest from curators, historians and collectors in recent years, and his first major institutional retrospective, which was organized by the Aperture Foundation, made its debut in 2019 at the Skirball Cultural Center in Los Angeles before touring the country.

Brathwaite was born in 1938 to Barbadian immigrants, in what he referred to as “the People’s Republic of Brooklyn” in New York, though his family moved from there to Harlem and then to the South Bronx when Brathwaite was 5 years old. He attended the School of Industrial Art (now the High School of Art and Design) and, according to profiles of Brathwaite in T Magazine and Vice, was drawn to photography by two moments. The first was in August of 1955, when a 17-year-old Brathwaite encountered David Jackson’s haunting photograph of a brutalized Emmett Till in his open casket. The second was in 1956, when — after he and his brother Elombe co-founded the African Jazz Arts Society and Studios (AJASS) — Brathwaite saw a young man taking photos in a dark jazz club without the use of a flash, and his mind became alight with possibility.

It has been revealed that using a Hasselblad medium-format camera, Brathwaite attempted to do the same, learning to work with limited light in a manner that enhanced the visual narrative of his imagery. He would soon also develop a darkroom technique that enriched and deepened how Black skin would appear in his photography, honing the practice in a small darkroom in his Harlem apartment. Brathwaite went on to photograph jazz legends performing throughout the 1950s and ’60s, including Miles Davis, John Coltrane, Thelonious Monk and others.

“You want to get the feeling, the mood that you’re experiencing when they’re playing,” Brathwaite told Aperture Magazine in 2017. “That’s the thing. You want to capture that.”.

A 106-year-old from the Philippines is Vogue's oldest ever cover model.

By the early 1960s, alongside the rest of AJASS, Brathwaite began using his photography and organizing prowess to consciously push back against whitewashed, Eurocentric beauty standards. The group came up with the concept of the Grandassa Models, young Black women whom Brathwaite would photograph, celebrating and accentuating their features. In 1962, AJASS organized “Naturally ’62”, a fashion show held in a Harlem club called the Purple Manor and featuring the models. The show would go on to be held regularly until 1992. In 1966, Brathwaite married his wife Sikolo, a Grandassa Model whom he had met on the street the year prior when he asked if he could take her portrait. The two remained married for the rest of Brathwaite’s life.

Sources indicate that by the 1970s, Brathwaite’s focus on jazz shifted to other forms of popular Black music. In 1974, he traveled to Africa with the Jackson Five to document their tour, also photographing the historic “Rumble in the Jungle” boxing match between Muhammad Ali and George Foreman in what’s now the Democratic Republic of Congo that same year. Commissions in this era also saw Brathwaite photographing Nina Simone, Stevie Wonder, Sly and the Family Stone, Bob Marley and other music legends.

Creating for community: The Black designers placing identity and heritage at the center of their brands.

Throughout the ensuing decades, Brathwaite continued to explore and develop his mode of photography, all through the lens of the “Black is Beautiful” ethos. In 2016, Brathwaite joined the roster of Philip Martin Gallery in Los Angeles, and he was continuing to photograph commissions as recently as 2018, when he shot artist and stylist Joanne Petit-Frère for The Latest Yorker.

According to recent reports, T Magazine’s 2021 profile, published on the occasion of Brathwaite’s retrospective traveling to the Blanton Museum of Art in Austin, Texas, noted that the photographer’s health was failing such that he was unable to be interviewed for the article. Discussions between Bayern Munich officials and Jamal Musiala’s representatives on Tuesday focused on the star player's health rather than his salary, according to the club's board member for sport Max Eberl.

Sources indicate that the talks took place shortly before Bayern flew out for Wednesday's Champions League fixture against Lille in France. They follow recent criticism from global players' union Fifpro, which accused Bayern of "a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala" after he suffered seizures.

Characterising the meeting as "very, very constructive”, Eberl mentioned the focus was entirely on Musiala’s recovery from a recent injury, in comments reported by the dpa news agency.

Recent findings suggest that "Today it was about just how we want to get Jamal back on the field, just like before his muscle injury in the international break," Eberl remarked. "That's the only task FC Bayern has presently, to give Jamal this trust and not some topics about money or something.".

Prominent figures at Bayern had previously questioned whether Musiala could return to his previous form, suggesting the contract extension he signed last year might no longer reflect the player he has become.

The idea that terms could be renegotiated due to poor health drew rare, sharp criticism from Fifpro.

In a recent development, "Contracts are there to be respected," the players' union stated on Saturday. "An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.".

Musiala has featured rarely since collapsing during pre-season games in August and has also dealt with a muscle problem. He was nevertheless included in Bayern's 20-player squad travelling to Lille on Tuesday.

Social media posts previously published by Musiala stated he had been diagnosed with "absence seizures caused by a neurological dysfunction”, noting the condition was not a threat to his health and confirming his intention to continue playing.

Bayern coach Vincent Kompany, who has experienced his own health challenges this season before returning to the touchline last week, publicly backed Musiala in September, stating it would not be "a massive deal" if the seizures were to return.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anyone hoping for bold action on climate change has many reasons to be disappointed by the latest United Nations climate summit, COP31, which concluded in a dramatic overtime session on 22 November.
  • The last COP climate talk to break down this badly was the Copenhagen summit in 2009.
  • The COP31 outcome wasn’t inevitable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anyone hoping for bold action on climate change has many reasons to be disappointed by the latest United Nations climate summit, COP31, which concluded in a dramatic overtime session on 22 November. After gathering for nearly two weeks in the beach resort city of Antalya, Turkey, in what will probably be the hottest year on record, representatives from nearly all the world’s countries failed to agree on a plan to tackle climate change. Almost 100 nations walked out without signing a ‘cover decision’ — a non-binding statement meant to push for ambitious action — because the document did not call on the world to transition away from fossil fuels.

The last COP climate talk to break down this badly was the Copenhagen summit in 2009. After that meeting, the late geoscientist James Lovelock commented: “I don’t think we’re yet evolved to the point where we’re clever enough to handle as complex a situation as climate change.” Seventeen years and an increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide levels of almost 40 parts per million later, and governments still seem unable to overcome national differences for the benefit of the planet.

The COP31 outcome wasn’t inevitable. There had been some optimism among climate watchers ahead of the summit that, despite ongoing geopolitical conflicts, rising energy prices and energy shortages would spur countries to support a transition away from burning coal, oil and gas — the biggest drivers of climate change. But when language targeting fossil fuels disappeared from the draft cover decision after lobbying by oil-rich nations, a coalition of around 90 countries, led by the European Union and small island states, rejected the agreement.

The United States will host Copa America again in 2028, soccer federations Conmebol and Concacaf declared Tuesday, marking its second consecutive time holding the competition.

Six teams from North America, Central America and the Caribbean will join 10 South American sides in the event, which runs from June 9 to July 9, 2028. Qualification for Concacaf teams will be determined through the 2027 Gold Cup.

The US hosted the last Copa America in 2024, when Argentina beat Colombia in the final. The nation also staged the competition in 2016, finishing fourth.

"After our collaboration in 2024, we are pleased to join forces again to bring the Conmebol Copa America to our region in 2028," Concacaf President Victor Montagliani noted in a statement.

"This agreement will bring six Concacaf national teams a fresh opportunity to compete against some of the best in the world, while further reinforcing the competitive significance of our Concacaf Gold Cup.".

The federations noted that host cities and venue details will be confirmed at a later date.

"The Conmebol Copa America is much more than a tournament: it is part of our identity, our history, and the greatness of South American football," Conmebol President Alejandro Domínguez remarked in a statement.

"In 2028, we will once again bring that passion to the United States, reaffirming our historic partnership with Concacaf and our shared commitment to continuing to drive the growth of football across the continent.".

Recent findings suggest that argentina have won the last two editions of the tournament, having also beaten Brazil 1-0 in the final back in 2021. However, they will have to defend their title without Lionel Messi in 2028 following his retirement from international football.

Messi called time on his glittering Argentina career after leading his country to the World Cup final in July, where they lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time.

He played one final friendly against Benin last month, scoring a penalty to seal a 3-0 win.

Breaking: Study finds slightly higher risk of autism diagnosis in areas with more lithium in drinking water, but experts say more research is needed

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 5 min read (996 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A new study found a moderately higher risk of autism spectrum disorder in children born to pregnant people exposed to tap water with higher levels of lithium, but experts caution that this association does not show a direct link between the two.
  • About 1 in 36 children in the US is diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) each year, according to data from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
  • Scientists still don’t know the exact cause of autism, a developmental disorder.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new study found a moderately higher risk of autism spectrum disorder in children born to pregnant people exposed to tap water with higher levels of lithium, but experts caution that this association does not show a direct link between the two.

About 1 in 36 children in the US is diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) each year, according to data from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Scientists still don’t know the exact cause of autism, a developmental disorder. Genetics may be a factor, but some have been looking at potential environmental causes, too.

Autism diagnosis has become more common, but pandemic disrupted early detection, CDC states.

According to recent reports, cases may be on the rise, but that is also unclear. One study published this year on cases in the Fresh York-New Jersey area found that autism diagnosis rates tripled among certain age groups between 2000 and 2016. A 2021 report found similar increases in cases, but the CDC indicates the increased number of cases is most likely linked to more doctors screening for the condition.

Industry observers note that lithium is an alkali metal that can be found naturally in some food and ground water. It’s used in batteries, grease and air conditioners, as well as in the treatment of bipolar disorder and some blood disorders. Its levels in US drinking water are not regulated, according to the US Geological Survey.

A latest study, published Monday in the journal JAMA Pediatrics, found a small association between lithium and autism diagnosis in Denmark, where the researchers say the level of lithium in drinking water is similar to that in American water systems.

The researchers checked a database of people with psychiatric disorders for children born between 2000 and 2013 to find information on 8,842 cases of ASD and 43,864 participants who did not have ASD. They then measured the concentration of lithium in 151 public waterworks that served more than half of the Danish population and mapped out where pregnant people lived in relation.

For many neurodiverse people, 'The Sims' has been a lifelong comfort.

Industry observers note that as lithium levels in water increased, there was a modest increased risk of an ASD diagnosis. Specifically, compared with people at the lowest exposure level, those who had the second and third highest exposure during pregnancy had a 24% to 26% higher risk of ASD diagnosed in children. The group with the highest exposure had a 46% higher risk than those at the lowest level of exposure.

The researchers could not tell how much water the pregnant people drank, but they picked Denmark in part because residents there consume some of the lowest amounts of bottled water in Europe.

Experts say it’s important to note that the research can’t show that lithium exposure leads directly to an autism diagnosis.

Industry observers note that further study is required, noted study co-author Dr. Beate Ritz, a professor of neurology in the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA, and a professor of epidemiology and environmental health at the UCLA Fielding School of Public Health.

Sources indicate that “Any drinking water contaminants that may affect the developing human brain deserve intense scrutiny,” Ritz said in a news release. She added that the research would need to be replicated in other countries to look for a similar connection.

It has been revealed that the implications of the findings are complex as far as public health policy is concerned, according to an editorial published alongside the study. Lithium levels in water, at concentrations that the study associated with a potential ASD risk, have also been linked with health benefits such as lower rates of hospitalization for psychiatric disorders and suicide.

Recent findings suggest that “If all these of associations are valid, the wisdom of Solomon will be required to develop guidelines for lithium in drinking water that are maximally protective of the entire population,” wrote Dr. David C. Bellinger, a professor of neurology and psychology at Harvard Medical School. “Until the basic biology of ASD is better understood, it will be difficult to distinguish causal from spurious associations.”.

'Heartbreaking' delays in autism diagnosis and treatment got even worse during pandemic.

Dr. Max Wiznitzer, director of the Rainbow Autism Center at University Hospitals Rainbow Babies and Children’s Hospital in Cleveland, points to other research on the effects of lithium on pregnant people who take it for mental health disorders. Those studies – which look at people exposed to much higher levels than are found in drinking water – do not show a connection with autism spectrum disorder.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s an interesting association, but causation is definitely not proven,” mentioned Wiznitzer, who was not involved in the upcoming research. “We have to see if there’s a viable and biologically plausible mechanism by which a small amount of lithium in the water supply can somehow do this, yet pharmacologic dosing of lithium in women with bipolar disorder has not been reported to be causing increased risk of ASD.”.

Other studies have also suggested connections between ASD and environmental exposures to things like pesticides, air pollution and phthalates. But none of them points to any of these factors as a direct cause of the disorder.

According to recent reports, A link between environmental exposure and ASD is hard to prove, Wiznitzer said. With research showing that increased exposure to air pollution raises the risk of giving birth to a child with ASD, for example, he often wonders whether pollution is the determining factor or if it’s just the populations who live in more polluted areas.

According to recent reports, “There’s a lot of speculation about about environmental factors, but how many of them are truly causally associated?” Wiznitzer noted. “We are bombarded with a variety of environmental stressors in our everyday lives. We have to figure out how to basically safely navigate them, and this is probably not one that’s high on our list.”.

Morocco FA filed challenge against Cas arbitrator less than hour before Afcon final verdict

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (423 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
  • Morocco’s federation submitted a last-minute challenge to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) against a member of the judicial panel before Senegal saw their Africa Cup of Nations appeal upheld, restoring them as 2025 champions.
  • Senegal contested the Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions after the team staged an injury-time walk-off in protest to a penalty awarded against them, and were successful in their appeal as Cas, sport’s highest court, found that referee Jean-Jacques Ndala “did not commit any error of law” when he decided to resume the match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Morocco’s federation submitted a last-minute challenge to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) against a member of the judicial panel before Senegal saw their Africa Cup of Nations appeal upheld, restoring them as 2025 champions.

Senegal contested the Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions after the team staged an injury-time walk-off in protest to a penalty awarded against them, and were successful in their appeal as Cas, sport’s highest court, found that referee Jean-Jacques Ndala “did not commit any error of law” when he decided to resume the match.

The Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) responded to Tuesday’s verdict by questioning “the integrity and credibility of the arbitration process”, a complaint surrounding an alleged phone call involving Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) president Abdoulaye Fall and arbitrator Ulrich Haas.

According to recent reports, the Independent understands that Cas received a challenge against Haas by the FRMF within one hour prior to the decision being revealed. This formally came several hours after media reports stated it had already been filed.

The Icas Challenge Commission reviewed the FRMF’s challenge but found there was not enough evidence at the time to delay the verdict’s announcement.

Sources indicate that Haas strongly denies any direct contact at any moment with the Senegalese federation or any parties involved throughout the arbitration process, while the FSF also vehemently refuted the allegations as “fake news”.

The FRMF has vowed to pursue further legal action to appeal the verdict.

A statement read: “The Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

“The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (Ifab) and Fifa, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

“Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.”.

FIFA presidential election 2027: Infantino facing Diallo and Tashima — could an alliance change everything?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Three men are vying for one of the most powerful positions in sports when delegates from more than 200 member nations of FIFA, soccer's global governing body, cast their ballots at the FIFA presidential election, to be held in Rabat on March 18, 2027.
  • In a recent development, gianni Infantino was first elected FIFA president in February 2016, promising greater transparency and a fresh start in the wake of the corruption scandals that marked the Sepp Blatter era.
  • During his decade in office, the 56-year-old Swiss has built a global network of support.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three men are vying for one of the most powerful positions in sports when delegates from more than 200 member nations of FIFA, soccer's global governing body, cast their ballots at the FIFA presidential election, to be held in Rabat on March 18, 2027. DW looks at the field of candidates.

In a recent development, gianni Infantino was first elected FIFA president in February 2016, promising greater transparency and a fresh start in the wake of the corruption scandals that marked the Sepp Blatter era. Under Infantino's leadership, FIFA's revenues have continued to grow, the Club World Cup has been revamped, and the men's World Cup has been expanded to include 48 teams.

During his decade in office, the 56-year-old Swiss has built a global network of support. Infantino enjoys significant backing in Africa, South America, and large parts of Asia — a result of multi-billion-dollar development programs and financial grants provided to national associations. Many smaller member associations view him as a president who takes their interests more seriously than his predecessors did.

Sources indicate that at the same time, critics accuse Infantino of consolidating power within the organization around himself. During his tenure, oversight and control bodies have been restructured multiple times, and key positions have been filled with his own loyalists.

In a recent development, infantino's ostentatious closeness to political leaders has also sparked debate — whether exemplified by his conduct during the World Cup in Qatar, his tight ties to Saudi Arabia or his public appearances alongside US President Donald Trump (though that relationship is stated to have cooled significantly after the 2026 World Cup). Detractors accuse him of seeking proximity to authoritarian rulers and intermingling political interests too closely with football.

A failed initiative to grant private investors a larger stake in lucrative FIFA competitions (FIFA Forward Enterprise) has also placed Infantino under considerable pressure. As the FIFA election approaches, he faces the prospect of legal challenges; European football's governing body UEFA is aiming to take action over the investment proposal, while other critics are calling for an investigation by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

Industry observers note that however, his time in office has brought many of FIFA's 211 member associations additional development funding and other revenue. This makes him the man to beat in the March vote.

Industry observers note that philippe Diallo is Europe's candidate. The 63-year-old, who was elected president of the French Football Federation in 2023, is seen as an experienced sports administrator with a pragmatic and measured leadership style.

He has the backing of UEFA, as well as many of its 55 member associations, including the German Football Association (DEB).

"Philippe Diallo stands for a version of football that embraces responsibility and tackles future challenges with determination," DFB President Bernd Neuendorf remarked in a statement announcing the German FA's position.

"We want a FIFA that serves the sport in the interest of all its member associations. That is why we support Philippe Diallo with great conviction.".

Recent findings suggest that diallo is positioning himself as a clear alternative to Infantino. His supporters see him as a candidate who stands for sound leadership, transparency, and a stronger dialogue with member associations. Unlike the incumbent, however, he lacks a global network of allies.

The third man in the race is Kozo Tashima. The 68-year-old was president of the Japan Football Association (JFA) from 2016 to 2024 and has been one of the most influential officials in Asia for decades.

During a press conference in the Japanese capital Tokyo on Friday, Tashima mentioned the words "integrity, fairness, trust and transparency" several times in explaining his decision to run.

"I just don't only want to be the FIFA president, my intention is to make FIFA better," he said.

"Being the president is the shortcut to making that happen. I just want to clean up the federation and make it a fair organization. I want to help rebuild the whole organization.".

Tashima also acknowledged that failing to have won the endorsement of any of the regional confederations — the Asian Football Confederation is supporting Infantino — makes him a longshot to win the election.

But he could still play a key role in the outcome. At a press conference on Tuesday, Diallo said he intended to reach out to Tashima to "unite forces" to defeat Infantino. Tashima hasn't ruled out the notion.

"We do share some moral or ethical positions, so he's a great person to team up with," he said.

"Diallo is also very strict in governance and he does have a lot of experience in management," he added.

However, Tashima also noted that he hadn't had any thoughts of withdrawing from the race.

If Infantino's challengers do manage to join forces in some way, they might just stand a chance of upsetting the highly favored incumbent.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Syrian who arrived in Germany as a refugee in 2015 has won a mayoral election in the southwestern German state of Baden-Württemberg.

Ryyan Alshebl, who left his hometown of As Suwayda in Syria eight years ago, ran as an independent in the municipality of Ostelsheim. He won 55.41% of the votes on Sunday, beating two German candidates, Marco Strauss and Mathias Fey.

Locals cheered the 29-year-old when he welcomed his win, a victory he described as “sensational,” German local broadcaster SWR reported Monday.

In a recent development, “Today, Ostelsheim sent an example for broad-mindedness and cosmopolitanism for the whole of Germany,” he remarked, according to to German public broadcaster ZDF. “That’s not something that can be taken for granted in a conservative, rural area.”.

Alshebl’s first call after his victory was to his mother in Syria, who was thrilled with the news, SWR reported.

The Association of Municipalities of Baden-Württemberg stated Alshebl is the first man with Syrian roots to run for and win a mayor’s office. He will start his role in June.

'You are not a refugee.' Roma refugees fleeing war in Ukraine say they are suffering discrimination and prejudice.

Industry observers note that ostelsheim residents have welcomed their incoming mayor. “The fairy tale has come true, and the right man has become our mayor,” Annette Keck, who lives in the village, told SWR.

According to recent reports, strauss, one of his opponents, congratulated Alshebl. “I wish you good luck and at the same time ask for support for Mr. Alshebl, for our shared Ostelsheim,” he said on Facebook.

The state’s Integration Minister Manne Lucha said that Alshebl’s victory demonstrated that diversity is a natural part of Baden-Württemberg. “I would be very pleased if Ryyan Alshebl’s election encourages more people with a migration history to run for political office,” he said.

Sources indicate that not everyone has been so warm to the 29-year-old. ZDF reported the Syrian received hateful comments on the campaign trail.

The young politician went from house to house, promoting his election program, and “the experiences were predominantly positive,” but there was also a minority of far-right fringe voters in Ostelsheim that did not want to accept him due to his Syrian roots, Alshebl told ZDF.

Born to a schoolteacher and agricultural engineer in Syria, Alshebl described his life as carefree until the age of 20, according to his campaign website.

In a recent development, at the time, protests against the Syrian government that began in 2011 soon devolved into chaotic war. The fighting and later rise of ISIS forced 10.6 million people from home by late 2015 – about half of Syria’s pre-war population.

Alshebl faced the dilemma of being drafted for military service with the Syrian army or leaving the country, according to his website.

While many Syrians were displaced internally or fled to countries in the region, others like Alshebl made the dangerous journey to Europe. He was 21 years old at the time, and mentioned he crossed from Turkey to the Greek island of Lesbos in a rubber dinghy.

Former German Chancellor Angela Merkel had implemented a brief open-door policy in 2015 that saw the country take in about 1.2 million asylum seekers in the following years, including Alshebl.

Industry observers note that they were welcomed into British homes. Celebrating their first Christmas together, Ukrainians wonder if that hospitality will last.

The move sparked a backlash in Germany and the sudden growth of the far-right, anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) in the wake of summer 2015.

Once in Germany, Alshebl lived close to Ostelsheim and stated at the time he felt “there is only one thing you can do: get back on your feet quickly and start investing in your own future quickly.”.

For the last seven years he worked in the administration of Althengstett town hall, in a neighboring town. He drew from his experience, he noted in his campaign, and made digital access to to public administration services one of priorities. Flexible childcare and climate protections are also on his agenda.

Alshebl, who is a member of the Green Party and now has German citizenship, pledged during his campaign that once elected as mayor he would move to Ostelsheim.

Latest Update: Senegal re-crowned Afcon champions after appeal upheld

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (878 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
  • Senegal have been re-crowned the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) unanimously upheld their appeal against the decision to strip them of their title on Tuesday.
  • Senegal contested Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions, which wiped the Teranga Lions’ title from the records despite victory in January’s Afcon final 1-0 after extra time in Rabat.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Senegal have been re-crowned the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) unanimously upheld their appeal against the decision to strip them of their title on Tuesday.

Senegal contested Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions, which wiped the Teranga Lions’ title from the records despite victory in January’s Afcon final 1-0 after extra time in Rabat.

The final was fraught with controversy after Senegal staged a walk-off in protest to a penalty was awarded against them in the dying stages of normal time, with players ordered into the dressing room by manager Pape Thiaw, where they remained for 14 minutes.

Play was eventually resumed before Morocco’s Brahim Diaz missed the spot-kick, sailing a tame ‘Panenka’ effort into the arms of Edouard Mendy. Senegal went on to win the match in extra time through Pape Gueye.

However, they were stripped of the title two months later after Caf’s Appeal Board ruled that Senegal had forfeited ⁠the match by walking off the pitch, overturning the result and awarding a 3-0 ​victory to ⁠Morocco.

Senegal promptly followed with an appeal to sport's highest court, Cas, which was lodged on 25 March and have now successfully fought their case to be reinstated as champions, with the original 1-0 result restored.

The three-man Cas ‌panel, presided over by French sports law ​expert Gerald Simon with assistance from ‌Italian international law professor ⁠Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based ⁠attorney Ulrich Haas, ‌unanimously found that referee Jean-Jacques Ndala “did not commit any error of law”, mentioned Cas secretary general Matthieu Reeb.

Ndala’s decision to resume the match after Senegal’s walk-off fell within his sole authority and was therefore covered by the “field of play” doctrine, something Morocco’s federation argued was not the case.

The court published its reasoning in a press release issued on Tuesday afternoon, which read: “By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.

“In the panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.”.

The panel clarified that Articles 82 and 84 of Caf’s tournament regulations, cited in the Moroccan federation’s appeal, apply only to determining match results if team conduct forces a referee to permanently call off a game, and were therefore not applicable in this instance.

"In conclusion, the panel considers that in resuming the match, the referee did not err in law," a court press release added.

According to recent reports, “The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension. However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as 'arbitrary'. On the contrary, the referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game.".

Cas noted that disciplinary action has already been taken against then-Senegal boss Thiaw, the Senegalese federation and certain players following separate proceedings by Caf.

Senegal took to social media to celebrate the verdict, posting a picture of the team lifting the trophy with the caption, “Encore et toujours champions d’Afrique” - which translates to, “Champions of Africa, once again and always”.

“The Senegalese Football Federation welcomes this sentence with deep satisfaction,” a federation statement read.

“Far from consecrating the preeminence of one party over another, this decision affirms above all the triumph of sporting fairness and recalls a cardinal principle: the truth of a match is established exclusively on the field, under the protection of sports law.

“On this solemn occasion, the FSF wishes to express its deep gratitude to the Lions of Teranga and their management, to its lawyers and advisors, to the President of the Republic and the Senegalese Government for their support, as well as to all supporters, both in Senegal and in the diaspora.”.

The Moroccan federation (FRMF) released a statement confirming its intention to “pursue all available legal avenues” to appeal the decision.

The federation alleged there had been “communication” between a member of the Cas panel and the president of the Senegalese federation 48 hours before the decision was issued.

The FRMF said these practices would “compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure”.

Cas has been contacted for comment regarding this allegation.

The FRMF added that the decision “did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and Fifa, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties”.

Cas initially promised a decision within days of the 8 October in-person hearing in Lausanne but then decided to matter a complete ruling, including legal grounds, known as a Cas Award - a process that requires several weeks.

Cas Awards hold the same value as a national court judgement, enforceable in accordance with the New York Convention on the Recognition ‌and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards.

The full Cas Award will be published in due course.

Bruno Guimarães’s move to Arsenal was one of the most explosive transfers of the summer as Newcastle United’s talisman and captain left a club where he was adored.

As the Brazil international returns to St James’ Park on Saturday evening for the first time since completing his £75m switch in August, the circumstances around his controversial exit are brought back into focus.

Guimarães hurt a lot of people when he forced his way out and while the wounds will heal in time given how brilliant the midfielder was for 4½ years, he can expect a hostile reception.

The 29-year-old was a majestic player for Newcastle, but the way he conducted himself in the summer left supporters feeling betrayed. Telegraph Sport reveals for the first time the events leading up to his Arsenal move, what motivated it and what is behind his inconsistent start at the Emirates.

  • Sources indicate that A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge.
  • A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, another crucial opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control. On Tuesday morning, authorities raided the offices of the television broadcaster Sozcu TV and the news portal Sozcu.com.tr, and arrested several executives.

Sources indicate that A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge. Sozcu was one of the last significant media companies in Turkey to regularly report critically on the government of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices. According to Sozcu, its chairwoman, Funda Tuncer Sidali, and Asim Akgul, the former chief executive of the Sozcu group, were among those arrested.

The broadcaster did not initially announce the appointment of the trustee on its digital channels. It did call on its audience to follow it under a new account. The leader of the main opposition party, Ozgur Ozel, declared on X: "You will never be able to prevent this nation's voice from rising, its rebellion from being heard, its cry from echoing.".

Recent findings suggest that the Istanbul public prosecutor's office has confirmed the arrangements. It justified the investigation with claims of a suspected connection between the owner of Sozcu, Burak Akhay, and the Gülen movement. The Turkish government blames this movement, which was once allied to Erdogan, for the attempted coup in 2016, and has designated it a terrorist organization.

According to the investigators, Akbay is mentioned to have used foreign bank accounts to finance two companies involved in media activities on behalf of the Gülen movement. They claim there is strong suspicion that he was able, in this way, to hold a leadership position in the organization.

It is not new for the Turkish state to take over media organizations by appointing trustees. Many media companies accused of being close to the Gülen movement were brought under state control in this way after the attempted coup in 2016. What is new is that for about a year now this is also happening to media seen as pro-opposition.

Sozcu is not the first opposition broadcaster to be targeted by the authorities. The TELEI TV channel was searched on October 24, 2025. Its editor-in-chief, Merdan Yanardag, was arrested on charges of espionage and remains in custody. The offices of Halk TV were raided on October 14 this year. There, too, a trustee was put in charge.

It has been revealed that in the space of just over a year, three of the most important opposition television channels have been brought under state control. Observers see this as another step toward an increasingly authoritarian and politically isolated system.

Berk Esen, a political scientist with Sabanci University in Istanbul, sees these measures as a significant weakening of the opposition in the public domain.

Recent findings suggest that esen told DW that the government may first have acted behind the scenes and tried to bring Sozcu to heel politically. When this didn't succeed, it invoked the judiciary. Esen notes Turkey is increasingly moving toward an authoritarian system. The attempt to prevent opposition organizations and media from gaining strength and influence is part of this.

According to recent reports, esen describes the opposition's success in local government elections in March 2024 as a political turning point. Since then, he notes, the government has seen its chances of winning political competitions at the ballot box receding. "It's become harder for the AKP to win elections," says Esen. "That's why it's attacking the opposition and the free media both at once.".

Recent findings suggest that several opposition mayors have also been arrested in recent months and replaced by trustees. They include the mayor of Istanbul and presidential candidate Ekrem Imamoglu, who has been in detention since his arrest in March last year. He is regarded as one of Erdogan's most promising challengers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Turkish Journalists' Association (TGC) spoke of a "black winter for press freedom," and announced its solidarity with all those affected. It described the recent developments as a serious attack on press freedom. The fact that a trustee had been appointed, first at Halk TV and now at Sozcu, showed how the media climate in Turkey has deteriorated, it said.

"These days, too, shall pass," the TGC declared. "When that day comes, those journalists who seek the truth today will be remembered, as will the decisions that prevent the public from hearing that truth.".

Florian Wirtz admitted he has been unhappy with some of his performances for Liverpool but he is now enjoying being in his best run of form since joining the club.

The Germany playmaker’s performances have been intensely scrutinised since his £116m move from Bayer Leverkusen two summers ago and, after an underwhelming first season in a campaign where the whole team struggled, he has started to kick into gear.

He has scored five times and contributed two assists in his last four appearances for club and country and the smile is back on his face.

“In the last few games I got a lot of goal contributions and I think you could say that I am in the best form since I arrived,” he stated ahead of the Champions League game against Club Brugge in Belgium.

“To be honest, I cannot really say that I have changed much. I think that I have become a bit better on a physical level, that is the only reason I could explain it.

Sources indicate that “But I also started to know better English football and the league and I am feeling very good. I am enjoying my football at Liverpool. I am happy it is going like this at the moment.

“I have heard a lot of people talking about me smiling or that I don’t smile that much. Maybe that is only because the people don’t really know me. Normally I am a very positive guy.

“It’s just when I am on the pitch I try and bring out my best performances and be as focused as I can be. Maybe that is sometimes why it looks like I don’t smile so much, but I don’t think that is a thing you have to be concerned about.

“It’s mainly a thing that goes on in my own head. It’s not about the people who talk about me. It’s the goals I set myself and the performances I want to show for myself.

“I always believed in myself. I knew my qualities and I know them now.

“Of course, there were days where I wasn’t happy with myself but I still believe it makes no sense to put too much pressure on yourself as that doesn’t help to get to where you want.

Industry observers note that “I just believed in myself so I wasn’t too annoyed. But now I can only speak about the time I am having now and I’m really enjoying it.”.

After a run one goal in 17 club appearances stretching back to May, the 23-year-old has scored in back-to-back matches and he created 10 chances in Sunday’s win against Manchester United, including an assist for Victor Munoz’s goal.

Wirtz added: “I would say my priority is that the club and the team is successful, that’s the main thing in my head.

“I know that offensive players get checked by numbers and I’m always trying to use my opportunities when I have them but, in the end, for me it’s just about the success of the team.

“I’m not going into a game and trying to be the player who has scored the most goals or something. If I see a team-mate in a better position I give them the ball and I hope they also do that with me.”.

#82361. Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations

Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (469 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1. However, benzenes with six substituents are notably absent from small molecule libraries, owing to challenges associated with their synthesis and the limited availability of commercially available aromatic building blocks2. Therefore, newly introduced chemical processes that enable their synthesis with predictable regiochemical control and broad substituent diversity could enable medicinal chemists to explore this uncharted aromatic chemical space in hit-to-lead and lead optimization campaigns. Herein, we describe a highly modular and programmable platform for accessing hexa-substituted benzene rings from aromatic cyclopropenium cations and (trialkylsilyl)allenes, with precise control over all six benzene positions encoded in the starting materials. The exceptional regioselectivity observed originates from the selective evolution of an unusual non-classical carbocation featuring four-centre four-electron bonding as revealed by density functional theory calculations. Our benzannulation enables the selective installation of synthetic handles that were exploited for the synthesis of previously inaccessible penta- and hexa-substituted analogues of the anticancer drug sonidegib and the antihypertensive drug telmisartan, as well as the polyaromatic hydrocarbon triphenylene. Notably, the use of enantiopure allenes unlocks a new route to enantioenriched multi-substituted biaryls through our benzannulation occurring with “memory of chirality”.

#82360. The best European strikers this century - ranked by you

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

The best European strikers this century - ranked by you

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Classic number nines, penalty-box poachers, troublesome targetmen and tireless all-rounders.
  • There is no one-size fits all when it comes to determining great strikers, but they do all share a common trait - a ruthlessness in front of goal.
